subject: Treatment of heterogametic X in multiple QTL model

messages.author: ae2b3be3e252125b
messages.subject: Treatment of heterogametic X in multiple QTL model
parts:
Hello,

Can someone explain to me how a hemizygous X chromosome is treated during a multiple QTL scan implemented with mqmscan()? I have a backcross data set of all males that are 100% genotyped, and I receive the following error when running mqmscan().

> mqmscan(mapthis3, verbose=TRUE)
INFO: Received a valid cross file type: bc .
INFO: Number of individuals: 808
INFO: Number of chromosomes: 1
INFO: Number of markers: 153
INFO: 0 Cofactors received to be analyzed
INFO: Number of locations per chromosome: 155
INFO: Dominance setting ignored (setting dominance to 0)
INFO: Starting C-part of the MQM analysis
INFO: recombination parameters are not re-estimated
INFO: Re-estimation of the genetic map took 0 iterations, to reach a rdelta of 1.000000
INFO: Prob=0.020 Alfa=0.020000
INFO: Prob=0.020 Alfa=0.020000
INFO: dimX: 1, nInd: 808
INFO: F(Threshold, Degrees of freedom 1, Degrees of freedom 2) = Alfa
INFO: F(5.468, 1, 807) = 0.020000
INFO: F(3.906, 2, 807) = 0.020000
INFO: Log-likelihood of full model = -8133.523
INFO: Residual variance = 0.230
INFO: Trait mean= 0.357; Trait variation = 0.230
INFO: mapQTL function called
INFO: log-likelihood of full model = -8133.523865
INFO: Number of output datapoints: 155
INFO: All done in C returning to R
Error in class(newres) <- c("scanone", class(newres)) :
attempt to set an attribute on NULL

Recombination in this cross is severely suppressed due to a large inversion. Maybe the resulting genetic map is distorted and resulting in an error? I've run into this error when running mqmscan() with all chromosomes, and also with the X alone. Additionally, I've run into this error when treating the phenotype as normally distributed (though it is not), and transforming it to binary. When running on all chromosomes, the X is dropped from the resulting model, graphs, etc. Lastly, there is severe segregation distortion in this cross due to inviability of some BC hybrid genotypes.

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Treatment of heterogametic X in multiple QTL model
parts:
mqmscan() seems to omit the X chromosome. As a result, if your cross consists of only the X chromosome, it gives an error as the output will be strictly NULL.

It seems that the X chromosome hasn't been implemented in mqmscan() at all.

karl
